mappings.note: Buildings, bridges and machinery as human-made resources - LO-1 is the only outcome that names the natural/human-made pair; LO-2 is about justifying use, which this does not ask.

Coal as the standard non-renewable example, which is the basis of the conservation case in LO-2. NOTE: no options or answer are stored, so 'natural resource' would also complete the stem; LO-1 would then apply.
Why resources are spread unequally - LO-1's uneven distribution, exactly.
Renewable resources, the category that makes judicious use possible - LO-2, not LO-1, which is about where resources sit on the earth.
A patent turning knowledge into something of value - what makes a thing a human-made resource, LO-1. The frame has no outcome for intellectual property.
Identifying a natural resource - the natural/human-made distinction of LO-1.
Technology as a human-made resource - LO-1.
'Environment' as everything living and non-living around an organism - the stock from which natural resources are drawn, LO-1.
Resources drawn from nature with little modification - the natural category, LO-1.
The definition of a resource itself - LO-1, the only outcome that deals with what resources are rather than how to use them.
How resources are classified - LO-1's natural and human-made categories.
What non-renewable means - the limit that the judicious-use argument of LO-2 rests on.
An example of sustainable development - LO-2's justification of judicious use, not LO-1's distribution.
What does NOT make a substance a resource - utility and value, LO-1's account of resources.
Human resource development through skills - a resource category, LO-1; the frame names natural and human-made resources but has no separate human-resource outcome.
Distribution is uneven because the underlying factors differ - LO-1 verbatim.
Resources that replenish quickly - the renewable category behind LO-2's conservation case.
